what: The hero illustration stage is driven by the wheel with document scroll locked. The title rises in 1s and the baseline drawing in 1s, and .5s later the swaying props and the scroll indicator rise in 1s (the indicator moves 15% up and down every 2s). Rolling the wheel makes the title vanish in 1s and turns on the mark layers. Rolled amount ÷ (screen height × layer count × .5) becomes progress, and each layer turns on in turn by progress×6−index. When progress reaches 1, the wide illustration covers in .3s and the stage recedes to .88x in 1s (on phones it approaches to 1.29x), then a white veil comes in over .3s, the body opens and the lock is released. At phone width a single push down finishes it

options.steps: Multiplier applied to progress (speed at which layers switch on), default 6
options.span: Wheel amount per floor (screen heights), default .5
options.zoom: Scale the stage recedes to at the end, default .88
options.fade: Duration for title, floor and props to rise (s), default 1
options.bob: Duration of one wobble of the scroll indicator (seconds), default 2

note: The stage size and position are given by the consumer (the original is a 3840:877 ratio, 114.6% of the screen width, centered). The picture layers inside the stage are overlapped by this part. The body stays hidden until the end. When finished it fires fx:done, so body entrance motion should be hooked after that. It also advances with the keyboard (↓ · PageDown · Space). From the second loop the original swaps in a pre-merged bottom image, but there is no visible difference, so the bottom is left as it is.
